pr.title: dataflow_const_prop: do not eval a ptr address in SwitchInt
pr.author: dianqk

issues.title: [ICE]: got a pointer where a ScalarInt was expected: alloc1
issues.body:
```rust
pub static mut G: i32 = 0;
fn myfunc() -> i32 {
    let var: *mut i32 = &raw mut G;
    if !var.is_null() {
        return 0;
    }
    return 0;
}
pub fn main() {
    myfunc();
}

```
**Reproduce command:**
```console
% rustc -Zmir-opt-level=3 test.rs
```

processing.reason: The historical wrong transformation is an ICE, not a runtime miscompilation: `scalar.assert_scalar_int()` panics on a `Scalar::Ptr`, so `DataflowConstProp` aborts with "got a pointer where a ScalarInt was expected" before emitting any optimized MIR. There is therefore no defined historical execution whose result can differ from the corrected execution. The added regression test is explicitly `//@ check-pass` and only checks that compilation succeeds instead of crashing. A function pair that returned different numeric values (for example by treating the pointer's allocation offset as 0 and choosing the `0` arm) would invent a pointer-to-int interpretation that the patch does not contain. The only source-grounded behavioral distinction is "old compiler panics / keeps no switch vs corrected compiler preserves the `SwitchInt`", which cannot be expressed as two Miri-clean Rust functions with genuinely differing defined runtime values.

analysis.originalLogic: In `DataflowConstProp`'s `handle_switch_int`, a `FlatSet::Elem(scalar)` result was treated as necessarily an integer scalar. The original logic was `let choice = scalar.assert_scalar_int().to_bits_unchecked();` followed by selecting one successor with `TerminatorEdges::Single(targets.target_for_value(choice))`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to collapse every constant-propagated `SwitchInt` discriminant that is a single scalar value into the corresponding single integer target, even when that scalar is a pointer rather than a `ScalarInt`. Calling `assert_scalar_int()` on such a pointer caused the ICE instead of preserving the switch. The corrected logic only collapses when `scalar.try_to_scalar_int()` succeeds; otherwise it keeps `TerminatorEdges::SwitchInt { discr, targets }`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR `SwitchInt` terminators whose discriminant is known by `DataflowConstProp` to be exactly one scalar (`FlatSet::Elem`), including pointer scalars arising from raw pointers or pointer-to-integer transmutes, not only integer scalars. The relevant source shape is a `match`/`switch` on a `usize` produced by `std::mem::transmute` of a raw pointer, or raw-pointer null checks after constant propagation.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in `DataflowConstProp`: `SwitchInt` constant folding must not assume every `FlatSet::Elem` scalar is a `ScalarInt`. A constant pointer scalar (for example from a ptr-to-int transmute) made the old code call `assert_scalar_int()` and ICE with "got a pointer where a ScalarInt was expected". The fix attempts `try_to_scalar_int()` and, on failure, leaves the `SwitchInt` intact.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` terminator's discriminant is constant-propagated to a single pointer scalar, then `DataflowConstProp` tries to convert it to an integer and choose a single successor.
preconditions: `DataflowConstProp` is enabled for the optimized MIR.
The switched-on value is represented as `FlatSet::Elem(scalar)`.
The scalar is a pointer rather than a `ScalarInt`, e.g. after a pointer-to-integer transmute or a raw-pointer null check.
pitfalls: Do not treat `FlatSet::Elem(scalar)` as proof that the value is an integer scalar.
Do not call `assert_scalar_int()` on a propagated scalar without checking for pointer provenance/shape first.
When integer conversion fails, preserve the original `SwitchInt` edges rather than dropping exploration with `TerminatorEdges::None`.
The test needs the specific pass combination; merely compiling without `DataflowConstProp` may not exercise this transformation.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test using `//@ check-pass` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+InstSimplify-before-inline,+DataflowConstProp`. Construct a static mutable global, take `&raw mut` to it, transmute the pointer to `usize`, and `match` that `usize` with at least a `0` arm and a `_` arm. This forces a `SwitchInt` on a pointer-derived value while exercising `DataflowConstProp`. A contrasting integer-only variant can verify normal single-target folding. No execution is needed; the test only checks that compilation succeeds rather than ICEing.
